name: Paper marbling
summary: A way to colour paper with pigment that floats on a bath of thick water. The maker combs the pigment into a pattern and lays a sheet on it.
how: Thicken water with a gum to make the size, and pour it into a shallow tray.
Float the pigments on the size with a brush; each drop spreads to a ring.
Draw the drops into veins with a stylus, a comb or a fan.
Alum the paper first so that the pigment takes.
Lay the sheet on the bath for one touch, lift it, and let it dry flat.

origin.note: Ottoman marbled paper appears in the margins of a Hâlnâma manuscript of 1539–40. Older Persian or Central Asian sheets are possible.

adoptions.via: Ottoman scribes and binders use marbled paper in the margins and the covers of manuscripts, and the craft grows into the art of ebru.
